title: Water Safety
hook: Drowning is fast and silent — no splashing, no shouting. The single best protection for a young child is an adult within arm's reach whenever there's water.
key_points: Young children can drown in an inch or two of water, quickly and silently — there's rarely the splashing people expect.
Use 'touch supervision': stay within arm's reach in the bath and at the pool, with eyes on the child, not your phone.
Empty buckets, tubs, wading pools, and coolers right after use, and never leave an open container of water unattended.
Fence home pools on all four sides with a self-closing, self-latching gate — and never leave a child alone near any water.
content_html: The hardest thing to internalize about drowning is that it doesn't look like the movies. The American Academy of Pediatrics emphasizes that it's fast and silent — there's rarely splashing or shouting — and that young children can drown in as little as an inch or two of water. That's why the protection that matters most is simply an adult close enough to act: "touch supervision," staying within arm's reach in the bath and at the pool, eyes on the child rather than a phone.
extra_html: Two more layers close the gaps. Around the house, empty buckets, tubs, wading pools, and coolers right after use and never leave an open container of water unattended. Around a home pool, the AAP recommends four-sided fencing that separates the water from the house and yard, with a self-closing, self-latching gate — a barrier that protects during the brief, inevitable lapses in supervision. Above all, never leave a child alone near any water. This is general guidance — take a hands-on infant first-aid/CPR class, and in an emergency call your local emergency number.

related.title: Childproofing the Home
related.hook: Anchoring furniture and TVs is the childproofing step parents skip most — and tip-overs are one of the deadliest home hazards for young kids. Then you cover the rest and redo it as baby gets mobile.

related.title: Sun Safety: Shade First for the Littlest
related.hook: Baby skin burns fast and shows damage for life. Under 6 months the rule is shade and clothing, not sunscreen; after that, sunscreen joins the hat and shade — not replaces them.

flashcards.prompt: What does drowning in a young child usually look like?

choices.text: Fast and silent, with little or no splashing
Loud splashing and shouting that's easy to hear
Something that only happens in deep water

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP stresses that drowning is quick and silent, and children can drown in just an inch or two of water.

flashcards.back_html: Staying within arm's reach of a young child in or near water — bath, pool, or open container — with your eyes actually on them, so you can reach them instantly.

flashcards.prompt: What kind of fence does the AAP recommend around a home pool?

choices.text: A four-sided fence with a self-closing, self-latching gate
A fence on three sides, with the house as the fourth side
No fence is needed if you supervise

flashcards.explanation_html: Four-sided isolation fencing separates the pool from the house and yard, and a self-closing, self-latching gate guards against brief lapses in supervision.
